- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (avg > 0.2) and model forecast is below recent 10-day moving average, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.2) — add 0.3–0.8% bias to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effects.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.3 in 3 days), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift, especially if price is trending upward.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 10-day low if sentiment is positive — model tends to underestimate upside potential in bullish sentiment windows.
